sources.label: json.loads documentation
sources.text: json.loads(s, ...) Deserialize s (a str, bytes or bytearray instance containing a JSON document) to a Python object. Changed in version 3.6: s can now be of type bytes or bytearray. The input encoding should be UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32.

controls.answer: According to the documentation: json.loads(s, ...) Deserialize s (a str, bytes or bytearray instance containing a JSON document) to a Python object. Changed in version 3.6: s can now be of type bytes or bytearray. The input encoding should be UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32.
json.loads takes not only str but also bytes and bytearray holding a JSON document, encoded as UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32.
json.loads accepts only str; bytes must be decoded before the call.
json.loads accepts bytes but rejects bytearray.

extraction_controls.answer: Here is the table as JSON: [{"id":1,"name":"a"},{"id":2,"name":"b"}] which keeps every field.

The compact form of the rows is:
[2]{id,name}:
  1,a
  2,b
That is all of them.
